text:
Evan: Hi all  just joined and trying to bootstrap on Windows 11 + WSL2. Followed the docs but hitting weird permission/symlink errors in devcontainer and my SSH setup uses Pageant/Putty. Any Windows-specific tips?
Priya: welcome Evan! :wave: Short checklist: enable WSL2 + Virtual Machine Platform, install Ubuntu 22.04 from Microsoft Store, and upgrade to latest kernel. Are you running VS Code Remote - WSL or Remote - Containers?
Evan: using Remote - Containers via Docker Desktop WSL backend. Docker starts but devcontainer build fails copying symlinks: "invalid argument" when running `ln -s`. Repo has many symlinks to scripts.
Mark: Windows host filesystem (ntfs) doesn't support some linux symlink semantics when mounted into WSL or a container. Best is to keep the repo inside the WSL distro (~/src) not on C:\Users. Clone the repo in WSL and open it from WSL filesystem in VS Code.
Evan: ah, repo was on C:\Users/Evan/projects. Moved it into `~/projects` in WSL and relaunching. Error changed to "Permission denied" when running `./scripts/setup.sh` in container.
Priya: check file modes and CRLF. If files were edited on Windows they might have CRLF and not be executable. Run `git config core.autocrlf input` in WSL and `git rm --cached -r . && git reset --hard` to normalize, then `chmod +x scripts/*.sh`. Also ensure your user in container has matching UID/GID or the mount options don't force root: `docker run -it --user $(id -u):$(id -g) ...` in build/test.
Evan: normalized line endings and chmod'd scripts; setup script progressed further. Now git operations inside container complain about credentials: host 1Password agent runs on Windows and Pageant is in use; container can't access keys.
Mark: with Pageant you can use ssh-agent forwarding via a socket proxy. On Windows, Win32 OpenSSH and Pageant are different. Easiest: install OpenSSH agent in WSL and add your key copy there, or use 1Password/ssh-agent forwarding. For Pageant specifically, use `npiperelay` and `win32yank`-style helpers or `wsl-ssh-pageant` to expose Pageant socket to WSL at `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`.
Evan: tried `wsl-ssh-pageant` and set `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/tmp/ssh-pageant.sock`, but inside docker container `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` points to a non-existent path. How do I forward agent into devcontainer?
Priya: mount the ssh agent socket into the container. In your `devcontainer.json` add a mount for the socket path (from WSL): "mounts": ["source=/tmp/ssh-pageant.sock,target=/ssh-agent,type=bind"] and "remoteEnv": { "SSH_AUTH_SOCK": "/ssh-agent" }. Also make sure the socket file is accessible (permissions).
Evan: added mount and env, but `ssh-add -l` in container is empty. WSL logs show `wsl-ssh-pageant` running as my user. Any permission quirks?
Mark: check that the socket is a named pipe vs unix socket; Pageant proxies sometimes create a Windows named pipe that doesn't behave as unix socket. `wsl-ssh-pageant` creates a unix socket; confirm with `ls -l /tmp/ssh-pageant.sock` in WSL. If the socket owner is root, chown to your user. Also restart the container after mounting so the socket is picked up.
Evan: chowned socket and restarted container, `ssh-add -l` now shows my key  nice. One more: devcontainer terminal complains `bash: asdf: command not found` though asdf is in my dotfiles and I installed it in WSL.
Priya: devcontainer image is a fresh container often without your home dotfiles. Either bake asdf into the devcontainer Dockerfile or mount your dotfiles/home into container (careful). Recommended approach: add an ENTRYPOINT or devcontainer postCreateCommand that runs dotfiles bootstrap: "postCreateCommand": "~/.dotfiles/install.sh" or include `RUN` steps in Dockerfile to install asdf and required plugins.
Evan: added `postCreateCommand` to run bootstrap script from a repo bind-mounted into container and now `asdf` appears. Last oddity: when editing with Windows editors sometimes file watchers in container flicker and VS Code shows "file changed on disk" a lot.
Mark: disable Windows antivirus real-time scanning for your WSL project folder or exclude the WSL distro volumes. Also avoid keeping repo on the Windows filesystem; WSL filesystem is much faster and less noisy. In VS Code settings, increase `files.watcherExclude` for node_modules and build dirs to reduce flakiness.
Evan: great tips. Everything is progressing: repo on WSL, agent forwarded, asdf available in container, line endings normalized. Thanks y'all! :tada:
